python_sqlite_connect.message0: open SQLite connection %1 database %2 timeout %3 seconds rows %4
python_sqlite_connect.tooltip: Open a named SQLite connection, first closing an existing connection with the same name. Cleanup closes the final connection; reconnecting does not commit pending work.

python_sqlite_execute.tooltip: Execute one parameterized SQL statement and return its cursor. A blank parameters input generates an empty tuple.

python_sqlite_query.tooltip: Run a parameterized query and return its cursor; fetch rows with the cursor result blocks.

python_sqlite_executemany.message0: connection %1 execute SQL %2 for parameter rows %3
python_sqlite_executemany.tooltip: Execute one parameterized SQL statement for every parameter row and return its cursor.

python_sqlite_fetchone.tooltip: Return the next row, or None when the cursor is exhausted.

python_sqlite_fetchall.message0: fetch all remaining rows from cursor %1
python_sqlite_fetchall.tooltip: Return a list containing every remaining row from the cursor.

python_sqlite_commit.tooltip: Commit the current transaction on the named connection.

python_sqlite_rollback.tooltip: Roll back the current transaction on the named connection.

python_sqlite_rowcount.tooltip: Read cursor.rowcount. SELECT statements normally report -1 until rows are consumed.

python_sqlite_lastrowid.tooltip: Read cursor.lastrowid; it may be None when no applicable INSERT has run.

python_sqlite_close.tooltip: Close the named connection and set its resource variable to None. Closing does not commit pending work.
